title: 2020 ESC Guidelines on sports cardiology and exercise in patients with cardiovascular disease
publisher: European Society of Cardiology / European Heart Journal
claims: The guidelines state that cardiac screening with family history, symptoms, physical examination and a 12-lead resting ECG should be considered for competitive athletes (Class IIa, Level C).

The guidelines state that among individuals with low to moderate cardiovascular disease risk, participation in all recreational sports should be considered without further cardiovascular evaluation (Class IIa, Level C).

The guidelines state that evidence for cardiovascular screening in athletes older than 35 years is limited and that screening in this group must target the higher prevalence of atherosclerotic coronary artery disease.

The guidelines state that routine screening for ischaemia with exercise testing in asymptomatic adults has a low positive predictive value and a high number of false-positive tests and is not recommended.
